content.text:
**Repaired finding submitted: deviation**, with a validated two-op redline (`ok:true`).

I changed my call after resolving the two definitions the verifier pointed at. Section 19 is strong, but there are two real gaps rather than a pure false negative:

1. **Duration (19.2)** — every Deliverable gets only "ninety days," spelled out in words. Our preferred position is 12 months for software and 90 days for services, so software Deliverables are short. The redline sets **twelve (12) months** for software Deliverables and **ninety (90) days** for all others. This closes the substantive gap and states the period in numerals/months, which also removes the ambiguity that kept tripping the period check. Hosted Services' continuous conformance throughout the subscription term is left untouched.

2. **Remedy base (19.4 + 1.5)** — the refund backstop is limited to "Fees paid for it," and **"Fees" means the Implementation Fee** only. As drafted the refund cannot reach subscription or service charges, which hollows out the repair/replace/refund remedy the playbook requires. The redline ties the refund to all amounts paid for the non-conforming item, and the comment offers broadening the Section 1.5 definition as an alternative.

Unchanged and compliant: 19.1 (professional/workmanlike plus conformity), 19.3 (Applicable Law, malicious code, no functionality diminution, open-source protection), the re-perform/repair/replace stack and its non-exclusivity carve-outs, and 19.5, which disclaims implied warranties only and expressly preserves express warranties, service levels, indemnities and remedies.

Fallback noted for negotiation: keep 90 days for all Deliverables if the refund fix is accepted.
